read_only reaches its gate only through the stream-path `req.plan_mode |= plan_gate`. /continue (continue_run with plan_mode=false) takes no agent_mode, and no test pins that a read_only run paused for approval resumes still in plan mode. Prove this before AGENT_MODES is switched on.

Under ZDR a read_only choice sets plan_mode before zdr_features::refusal (sse.rs ~1843), so the turn is refused as plan_mode. This is consistent but untested at stream level, and the matrix row agent_mode_resolves_identically_under_zdr does not exist yet.
read_only combined with execute_granted is refused as invalid_request ('execute_granted and plan_mode are mutually exclusive'), not with a mode-specific code. Fail-closed but opaque to the composer.

read_only on a plain (non-agentic) chat turn sets plan_mode, which writes the durable run plan mode, and on the openai-codex-subscription route normalize refuses plan_mode without agentic. Confirm both behaviours are intended for plain chat.
An unknown agent_mode on the stream path is a typed SSE error frame (HTTP 200); only the unary /invoke returns the plan's HTTP 400. The owner should confirm this convention.

ask_first and auto state rung Unspecified, so a thread grant (for example WorkspaceWrite) still applies under them, and a mode is not a ceiling on the grant. This needs an owner call against DEC-15/WS25-D6 before S9.
Lockdown covers only new agentic stream turns: continuations (/continue and the park form) never consult preset.do_runs, so S9 must enforce it there too.

The ordering guard in agent_mode_resolution_test is a source-text find over sse.rs (resolve before normalize_stream, LOCKDOWN_CODE before fn spawn_run_dispatch). It is brittle and proves no behaviour. A request-level stream test of the lockdown and unknown refusals would be stronger.
